text: Fine linear scratch on a painted or polished surface. Review if it crosses a functional seal, connector, or marked inspection zone; otherwise compare with the cosmetic acceptance standard.
Several parallel scratches near an exposed edge can indicate handling or fixture contact. Inspect the adjacent surface and check the part orientation in the fixture.
Deep groove with visible substrate exposure is a high severity surface defect. Hold the part for quality review and check for sharp edges or corrosion risk.
Shallow hairline mark that is visible only under reflected light. Confirm under the plant's standard inspection lighting before rejecting.
Visible crack in a structural area is a critical defect. Quarantine the part and escalate to quality engineering; do not approve based on image review alone.
Crack extending from a hole, fastener, or corner may propagate under load. Fail the part and inspect the batch for the same pattern.
Short surface indication near a seam may be a crack or a molding line. Use a second view or manual inspection before disposition.
A line that interrupts the material surface and branches at its end is consistent with cracking. Stop the line if repeated across parts.
An empty required mounting point or vacant connector position suggests a missing component. Fail the part and verify the assembly step and feeder.
A required fastener absent from a visible hole is an assembly defect. Hold for rework and inspect torque or pick-and-place records.
A partially hidden component cannot be confirmed from one angle. Mark for manual inspection or capture another view rather than assuming it is absent.
A missing seal, clip, or safety-retaining part can affect function. Fail and route to the assembly station for correction.
Localized inward deformation on a flat panel is a dent. Check depth and location against the product cosmetic limit; inspect packaging and handling.
A dent that distorts a mating surface or mounting plane can prevent assembly. Fail the part and verify the fixture and press settings.
Foreign material or residue on a functional surface requires cleaning or review. Do not confuse glare or a shadow with contamination.
Small color or gloss variation may be acceptable if it falls within the approved visual standard. Compare under controlled lighting and include a reference sample.
If the product is blurred, poorly lit, partly outside the frame, or obscured, request a new image or manual inspection. Do not issue a confident pass from inadequate evidence.
Reflections can resemble scratches and shadows can resemble missing parts. Use diffuse lighting or another angle when the image is ambiguous.
Visual AI output is a recommendation. Apply the approved inspection plan and have a qualified inspector make the final accept, rework, or reject decision.
When similar defects appear repeatedly, record the batch and machine context and alert the line lead. A single image does not establish a process root cause.
